framework.name: JISC Building Digital Capabilities: Individual Framework
key_principles: Digital Proficiency & Productivity sits at the centre, overlapping all other elements
No one will have all capabilities; the framework is aspirational and contextual
AI literacy is integral to digital capability (JISC February 2026 guidance)
The framework can be adapted for any role, subject or educational context
Discovery Tool provides self-assessment mapped to Developing/Capable/Proficient levels

cross_reference_frameworks.name: JISC AI Maturity Model for Education

aspects.name: Digital Proficiency and Productivity
aspects.description: The ability to use digital devices, networks, applications, software and services. How you use digital skills to accomplish tasks effectively and productively.

sub_elements.name: Digital Proficiency
sub_elements.description: Ability to use digital devices, networks, applications, AI, software and services; confident adoption of new tools; capacity to deal with problems.

sub_elements.name: Digital Productivity
sub_elements.description: Using digital tools and services to carry out tasks effectively; choosing the right tools for each task including AI; adapting tools to personal needs.

aspects.name: Digital Creation, Problem-Solving and Innovation
aspects.description: Digital production of content, using digital evidence to solve problems and make decisions, and willingness to try new practices with digital technology including AI.

sub_elements.name: Digital Creation
sub_elements.description: Digital production of content including AI-generated content; understanding different digital production processes.

sub_elements.name: Digital Research and Problem-Solving
sub_elements.description: Using digital evidence including AI-generated evidence to solve problems, make decisions and answer questions.

sub_elements.name: Digital Innovation
sub_elements.description: Willingness to try new practices with digital technology including Generative AI; assessing benefits, risks and accessibility.

aspects.name: Digital Learning and Development
aspects.description: Learning in digital settings and through digital media. Includes digital teaching practices for those in teaching roles.

sub_elements.name: Digital Learning
sub_elements.description: Learning effectively in technology-rich environments; using digital networks for CPD; reflecting on digital practices.

sub_elements.name: Digital Teaching
sub_elements.description: Teaching effectively with digital tools and in digital environments. For Teacher profile, covers eight areas of digital teaching practice.

aspects.name: Information, Data and Media Literacies
aspects.description: Finding, evaluating, managing and sharing digital information, data and media content including AI-generated content.

sub_elements.name: Information Literacy
sub_elements.description: Finding, evaluating, managing and sharing information in digital environments.

sub_elements.name: Data Literacy
sub_elements.description: Understanding and working with data including collection, analysis, interpretation and visualisation.

sub_elements.name: Media Literacy
sub_elements.description: Critically reading, creating and evaluating media content including AI-generated media.

aspects.name: Digital Communication, Collaboration and Participation
aspects.description: Communicating effectively in digital media, collaborating in digital teams, and participating in digital communities.

sub_elements.name: Digital Communication
sub_elements.description: Communicating effectively in digital media and spaces; designing digital communications including using AI.

sub_elements.name: Digital Collaboration
sub_elements.description: Participating in digital teams using shared tools including AI-powered collaboration tools.

sub_elements.name: Digital Participation
sub_elements.description: Participating in digital communities, civic engagement and professional networks.

aspects.name: Digital Identity and Wellbeing
aspects.description: Managing professional digital identity and presence, and maintaining health and wellbeing in digital and AI-mediated environments.

sub_elements.name: Digital Identity Management
sub_elements.description: Building and managing professional digital identity, reputation and presence.

sub_elements.name: Digital Wellbeing
sub_elements.description: Managing health, safety, relationships and work-life balance in digital environments; using technology aligned with values.

progression_levels.name: Developing
progression_levels.description: Building awareness and early skills. Interest in AI and digital tools is forming. Basic capabilities developing through guided exploration and initial experimentation.
progression_levels.target: Foundational awareness and active exploration of AI and digital tools within existing workflows
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Develop understanding and build practical skills through guided experimentation with AI tools relevant to role

progression_levels.name: Capable
progression_levels.description: Competent and confident. Systematic integration of digital and AI tools into professional practice. Able to select appropriate tools, evaluate outputs, and work independently.
progression_levels.target: Routine, informed AI-augmented practice integrated into professional workflows
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Demonstrate confident, systematic and responsible application of AI within professional domain

progression_levels.name: Proficient
progression_levels.description: Strong, advanced practice. Leading and mentoring others. Shaping institutional and sector approaches. Strategic perspective on digital and AI capability.
progression_levels.target: AI-enhanced practice as default; strategic use; mentoring others; sector leadership in AI innovation
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Lead AI integration, shape sector practices, and champion ethical and inclusive AI adoption

competency_blocks.name: Digital Proficiency and Productivity at Developing
competency_blocks.description: What digital proficiency and productivity looks like at the Developing level.
curricular_goals: Understand what AI is and how it relates to existing digital tools and services
Recognise where AI features are already present in everyday tools
Experiment with AI tools to enhance personal productivity
Develop habits for evaluating AI tool outputs
learning_objectives: Identify AI-powered features in tools they already use
Describe the basic concept of generative AI
Access and use institutional platforms and services
Use AI assistants for drafting, summarising or organising content
Evaluate AI-generated outputs for accuracy and fitness for purpose
Configure AI tools to support personal workflow preferences
contextual_activities: Try an AI assistant for a simple productivity task
Complete AI awareness module in Discovery Tool
Identify AI features in Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
Use Copilot to draft meeting notes or summarise documents
Compare AI-generated output with manual approach for a routine task
Explore AI features in specialist professional software

competency_blocks.name: Digital Proficiency and Productivity at Capable
competency_blocks.description: What digital proficiency and productivity looks like at the Capable level.
curricular_goals: Integrate AI tools systematically into professional workflows
Make informed decisions about when AI adds value and when it does not
learning_objectives: Select appropriate AI and non-AI tools for different professional tasks
Manage data privacy and security when using AI tools
Support colleagues in basic AI tool adoption
contextual_activities: Build an AI-augmented workflow for a recurring professional process
Conduct a personal AI tool audit identifying where AI helps and where it hinders
Deliver a peer demonstration of an effective AI workflow

competency_blocks.name: Digital Proficiency and Productivity at Proficient
competency_blocks.description: What digital proficiency and productivity looks like at the Proficient level.

contextual_activities: Lead a team workshop on AI-enhanced productivity
Contribute to an institutional AI tool evaluation process
Develop documentation for an AI-augmented departmental process
Publish a case study on AI-enhanced professional practice
Contribute to sector working group on AI in professional practice

cross_cutting_themes: AI literacy across all six elements
metadata.implementation_notes: JISC has not published explicit BDC x AI level crosswalks. These competency blocks are synthesised by combining BDC element descriptions with AI maturity level descriptors, informed by the Discovery Tool AI question sets (January 2024) and AI literacy definitions. The Discovery Tool's 3-level scale maps as: Developing = AI Levels 1-2, Capable = AI Level 3, Proficient = AI Levels 4-5.
